steps.what: Review the actual nuclear equipment design brief, controlled requirements, existing drawings and applicable engineering constraints, clarifying missing or conflicting requirements with their owners.
Design or develop nuclear equipment by evaluating concepts and engineering evidence, choosing design features and resolving interfaces with specialist colleagues within the existing design remit.

Develop the design drawings and supporting record in engineering design software {OTHER}; configure native drawing references and revision views to reduce repeated reference assembly while retaining all substantive modelling and explanation.
Check the complete equipment design record against its requirements, assumptions, interface evidence and revision references, resolving discrepancies before storing this engineering draft.
Commit the checked engineering draft in the existing engineering design repository {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native drawing-reference and revision views in engineering design software {OTHER}. Keep concept selection, substantive design and evidence checks with the engineer; storing the draft does not authorise construction or operation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Design records can repeat controlled drawing and revision references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference views can reuse existing controlled design links.
tasks.still_hard: Establish that a design satisfies its actual requirements and interfaces.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsupported assumptions and reconcile specialist evidence.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less record assembly with unchanged engineering responsibility.

evidence.claim: Native engineering reference and revision features can reduce repeated record assembly without validating a design.

assumptions: Boundary is this engineer's design contribution through its stored draft; independent verification, formal release, construction and operational controls remain existing downstream work, with no saving or transfer claimed. Shares are illustrative.

Requirements owners supply equipment identity, requirement IDs/revisions, interface constraints and approved source references. Engineer verifies and resolves gaps in s1 and develops actual design choices in s2-s3. Missing metadata requires original-document work, counted there; no free model-ready design is assumed.

Native reference configuration precedes code. Only repeated reference assembly loses time; actual design modelling and review retain effort. Existing solver runtime earns no labour credit. s4 is the ordinary completed-draft check, not an additional self-approval activity; edits invalidate the requested commit gate.
research_questions: Which drawing-reference actions are manually repeated today?

already_counted.description: Requirements review, design, retained assembly, final check and commit remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Maintain reference profiles and test revision behaviour.

approvals.approved_version: Final engineering draft checked in s4, not a release for construction

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 6.25 less 1 upkeep gives 5.25. Upper range 5 removes repeated reference assembly; zero where current native views already suffice.

tasks.short: Monitor nuclear operations for unsafe practices

steps.what: Retrieve the relevant operating records, controlled requirements and current facility status in the existing plant information system {OTHER}; configure native equipment and time-window views to reduce repeated lookup, checking source freshness and coverage.

Monitor nuclear facility operations through direct observation, original records and discussions with responsible personnel, identifying actual design, construction or operating practices that may violate requirements or jeopardize safety.

Evaluate the observed practices against applicable safety regulations, laws and controlled requirements, resolve uncertainty with relevant specialists and determine which concerns require the existing escalation process.

Write the actual monitoring findings in the existing plant issue system {OTHER}, preserving source references and unresolved concerns, then check the completed entry for factual accuracy and appropriate routing.
Commit the checked final monitoring entry to the existing plant issue system {OTHER} and its normal internal issue queue.

tasks.design: Configure read-only native views in the plant information system {OTHER} to reduce repeated source lookup. Keep observation, compliance interpretation and the actual issue record; this view neither controls the plant nor replaces existing alarms or escalation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant historical and requirement records may require repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source views can filter equipment and time without deciding safety compliance.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise a dangerous practice despite incomplete or apparently normal data.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge assumptions using actual plant context and specialist discussion.
tasks.altitude: Less lookup with unchanged monitoring and escalation duties.

reach.role: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors

evidence.claim: Read-only plant information views can reduce repeated record retrieval while compliance assessment remains expert work.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring through the normal internal findings record; emergency actions are task 5385. Shares are illustrative. Existing issue-queue routing is part of the one record commit, not an invented separate message or transport saving.

Plant records supply equipment ID, timestamps, record status and original source links; controlled documents supply requirement IDs and revisions. Engineer checks freshness and gaps in s1. Unavailable records require direct source inspection or personnel clarification in s1-s2, retained in their effort.

Native views are tested first. No saving is claimed for existing telemetry runtime, physical observation, interpretation, writing or the save. s4 includes the ordinary final-entry check, with no added self-approval labour; edits invalidate a1. Any urgent concern follows the existing immediate human escalation procedure without waiting for this record.
research_questions: Can existing views reduce retrieval without concealing stale or absent records?

already_counted.description: Source verification, direct monitoring, evaluation, actual entry and commit remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Check source-view coverage and broken reference links.

approvals.approved_version: Final monitoring entry and normal issue routing checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 6 less 1 upkeep gives 5. Upper case removes repeated source navigation only; zero where native views already provide it.

tasks.short: Initiate emergency corrective action or shutdown orders

steps.what: Assess the actual emergency information with the responsible operating personnel and applicable approved emergency procedure, checking source reliability and immediate uncertainties.

Decide the corrective action or plant shutdown order within the engineer's actual emergency authority, formulate the exact instruction and recipient, and check it against the assessed situation and approved procedure before communicating it.

Initiate corrective actions or order plant shutdowns by communicating the checked instruction to the authorised operating personnel over the existing emergency voice channel, obtaining acknowledgement and correcting any miscommunication immediately.

Record the actual instruction, time, recipient, acknowledgement and known response in the existing emergency log {OTHER} when operationally appropriate, then check the completed factual entry against the actual event.
Commit the checked emergency log entry in the existing emergency log {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Retain the existing human emergency procedure and voice communication. The actual instruction and the later factual emergency log remain separate; no new software or automation is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Emergency action requires immediate situational judgement within existing authority.
tasks.enabler_now: No new enabler is claimed; existing communications and log are sufficient.
tasks.still_hard: Act on incomplete information without delaying the required response.
tasks.human_edge: Take accountable emergency decisions and confirm shared understanding.

ambition.what: No additional shutdown or control authority.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the emergency response duties.

reach.role: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors
reach.task: Review an emergency communication after the event

evidence.claim: Emergency instruction, acknowledgement and factual logging are distinct human activities; ordinary record storage does not eliminate the response work.

assumptions: Boundary is the authorised engineer's assessment, instruction and actual log. Plant control execution belongs to operating personnel and is not claimed as saved or transferred labour. Shares are illustrative for an actual emergency, not incident frequency.

Operating personnel and observations supply actual condition, source and time in s1. Engineer establishes the exact instruction, recipient and authority in s2, with direct clarification counted in s1-s3. No automatic command or fabricated plant-state summary is used.

Native communication and emergency-log functions were considered; after splitting the actual report/write and command, no new removable manual duplication was found. Log writing and the real same-system save retain full time. No software change means zero incremental upkeep.

s2 is immediate normal instruction formulation/check, not an added approval queue or delay. a1 binds that specific instruction and recipient; a changed instruction requires the existing immediate human check again. s4 checks the actual completed log for a2, with no added self-approval activity. Logging never precedes or delays urgent response.
research_questions: Does the existing division of emergency roles match this focal-role boundary?

already_counted.description: Emergency assessment, instruction decision and delivery, actual log and commit remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: No change is proposed, so no additional upkeep is introduced.

approvals.approved_version: Specific immediate instruction and recipient formulated and checked in s2
Actual final emergency log entry checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All current emergency response and actual recording remain. No removed duplicate entry or changed human step has been established.

tasks.short: Examine accidents for preventive design evidence

steps.what: Examine accidents through actual site evidence and preserved records, verify provenance and distinguish direct observations from later interpretations without altering original evidence.
Interview relevant personnel about the accident and clarify the actual sequence and uncertainties, checking claims against available evidence rather than treating recollections as established facts.

Assemble accident data and its source-linked timeline in incident investigation software {OTHER}; configure native timestamp and source-reference views to reduce repeated sorting and lookup, checking time bases, missing events and conflicting records.
Evaluate the accident evidence for its relevance to preventive measures, distinguish causal hypotheses from supported findings and identify unresolved questions for design colleagues.

Write the factual accident examination note and qualified design-relevant findings in incident investigation software {OTHER}, then check the completed note against original evidence and its stated uncertainties.
Commit the checked final examination note in incident investigation software {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure source-linked chronology views in incident investigation software {OTHER}. Reduce repeated sorting while retaining evidence examination, interviews, causal interpretation and actual findings writing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence chronology can require repeated navigation and timestamp sorting.
tasks.enabler_now: Native investigation views can display explicit timestamps with source links.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting clocks, missing evidence and uncertain causation remain.
tasks.human_edge: Separate a plausible explanation from a supported finding.

ambition.what: No automatic causal or preventive-design decision.

tasks.altitude: Less chronology assembly; investigation responsibility stays the same.

reach.role: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors

evidence.claim: Timestamp and source-reference views can reduce chronology assembly without establishing accident causation.

assumptions: Boundary covers the engineer's accident examination through its actual internal note, not emergency response or final preventive design approval. Shares are illustrative.

Original record owners supply event IDs, timestamps, clock/time-zone context, equipment IDs and preserved source links. Witnesses supply actual accounts, obtained in s2. Engineer checks provenance in s1 and time conflicts in s3. Missing fields require source inspection and direct clarification counted in those steps; no inferred events are inserted as facts.

Native chronology views precede code. Only repeated sorting and lookup lose time; original evidence collection, interview, diagnosis, note writing and save keep their effort. Existing ingestion runtime earns no labour credit. s5 contains the ordinary completed-note check, not added approval work; edits invalidate the commit gate.
research_questions: How much actual manual sorting remains after existing investigation views?

incremental.description: Maintain chronology fields and test reference and clock displays.

approvals.approved_version: Final examination note and source references checked in s5
